    # RoomieOS — Product Requirements Document
    
    **Version:** 1.0 · **Project:** ENTI 407 Creation Project · **Target:** Friday, 27 November 2026
    **Product type:** Interactive, client-side prototype (not a deployed multi-user service)
    **Status:** Approved product decisions; implementation-ready
    
    ## 1. Product summary
    
    **Tagline:** Your shared home, organized.
    
    RoomieOS is a lightweight household workspace for **university students living with roommates in apartments or residence units**. It combines household chores, shared expenses and house agreements in one understandable interface. A roommate chooses their profile from a switcher and can see their responsibilities alongside household-wide information.
    
    **Core problem:** Shared households coordinate through fragmented group chats, memory and spreadsheets. Tasks get forgotten, purchases are hard to split, and agreed expectations are difficult to find.
    
    **Value proposition:** One place to see who is doing what, who owes whom, and what the household agreed to—without requiring a complicated setup.
    
    **Prototype disclosure:** There is **no authentication or shared backend**. The profile switcher simulates perspective only; it is not identity verification. Data is saved **only in the current browser**, never synchronized between roommates/devices. Use honest language in the app and presentation.
    
    ## 2. Outcomes and success criteria
    
    The MVP succeeds when a first-time visitor can:
    
    1. Open a public URL without signing in, and choose between a realistic sample household and starting with an empty one.
    2. Manage a household of **2–5 active roommates** with names and avatars.
    3. Create, edit, complete, skip, rotate and remove chores; see them in list and Kanban views; inspect completion history.
    4. Record expenses with **multiple payers** and **equal, percentage or fixed-amount splits**; see correct simplified balances; settle or reopen an expense.
    5. Add, edit and remove simple house agreements.
    6. Use a dashboard that combines the selected roommate's information with the overall household picture.
    7. Refresh the page and find all changes preserved locally, including settings and profile selection.
    8. Use the app on laptop and phone without broken controls or layout.
    
    **Assignment deliverables (per supplied ENTI 407 guide):** live/preview link; <=5-minute user-perspective video; complete dated prompt log, with PRD and design appendices if helpful. App quality criteria: usefulness, usability, functional persistence and interactions, lack of bugs, innovation and visual polish.
    
    ## 3. Explicit boundaries
    
    ### In scope (must ship)
    - One household per browser; first-run choice between sample data and an empty household.
    - Household name and household currency; **2–5 active roommates**; avatars as preset icon/emoji/initials or optional uploaded photo.
    - Roommate perspective switcher (non-authenticated).
    - Dashboard with personal and household summaries; **no activity feed**.
    - Chores CRUD, notes, due dates, assignment, statuses (pending/completed/skipped), list + Kanban, overdue indication, manual next-person rotation, completion history.
    - Expenses CRUD; categories and optional notes; multiple payers; three split methods; simplified outstanding balances; whole-expense settled/open state.
    - Simple agreements CRUD.
    - Local persistence, sensible sample data, destructive-action confirmations, reset and start-over flows, accessible responsive UI.
    
    ### Out of scope (do not build unless explicitly requested)
    Authentication, invitations, cross-device or real-time collaboration, database/server, API integrations, notifications, payment processing, chat, AI features, scheduled/background chore recurrence, recurring expense automation, foreign exchange conversion, partial settlements, receipt uploads, audit-grade finances, native mobile apps, multiple households, analytics, or a full permission model.
    
    ### Recommended implementation constraints
    Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Lucide icons (`lucide-react`); `localStorage`; no network calls required for application behavior. Deploy as a static site on Vercel. Prefer small readable functions to elaborate architecture.
    
    ## 4. Information architecture and user journeys
    
    **Navigation:** Dashboard / Chores / Expenses / Agreements / Settings. Household name and roommate switcher always accessible; Settings holds roster, currency, and reset.
    
    ### Journey A — First-time visitor
    1. The app has no saved data. Show a focused welcome setup with **Try sample household** and **Start from scratch**.
    2. **Sample**: initialize 3 named roommates with varied avatars, 4–6 chores across statuses, 3–4 valid expenses including a multi-payer example, and 2–3 house agreements. Pick one roommate as active.
    3. **From scratch**: ask for household name, currency, and **at least two roommate names** (avatar optional). Start with no chores, expenses or agreements. Select first roommate.
    4. Persist the chosen household and profile. Never overwrite changes on subsequent visits.
    
    ### Journey B — Manage chores
    1. Open Chores, switch between list and Kanban.
    2. Create a chore with required title, assignee, due date; optional notes.
    3. Edit or remove it; mark Pending, Completed or Skipped.
    4. On completion, record who completed it (the selected profile) and when.
    5. On rotation, assign the **next active roommate in household roster order**, wrap around, reset status to Pending and request/offer a new due date. Preserve prior completion events.
    6. Overdue applies only to Pending chores with due dates earlier than the current *local calendar date*.
    
    ### Journey C — Record a shared expense
    1. Create an expense: description, positive amount, date, category, optional notes.
    2. Add **one or more payers**, each with a contribution amount. Contributions must add exactly to total.
    3. Choose participants, then split method: **Equal**, **Percentage**, or **Fixed amounts**. Participants' shares must add exactly to total.
    4. Save, view expense breakdown, and inspect **Who owes whom** on Expenses.
    5. Mark an expense **Settled** only when its obligations have actually been handled outside the app; this removes its amounts from outstanding balances while preserving it in history. A settled expense can be reopened.
    
    ### Journey D — Switch perspective and maintain household
    1. Switch profile without logging in. Dashboard's **My chores** and **My balance** update immediately; shared household information does not change.
    2. Rename household, edit/add/remove roommates in Settings, and change currency only under the currency safeguards below.
    3. Reset sample data with confirmation, or choose Start over to return to first-run choice.
    
    ## 5. Functional requirements and acceptance criteria
    
    Requirements use `FR-*`. Each acceptance criterion should be manually testable and, where possible, covered by a unit/component test.
    
    ### 5.1 Setup and persistence
    
    **FR-01 — First-run choice**
    - With no valid stored state, the welcome screen offers Sample or Empty; neither silently chooses for the visitor.
    - Sample data is internally consistent; Empty creates an otherwise blank household after entering a name, currency and 2–5 roommates.
    
    **FR-02 — Local persistence**
    - All changes to household, selected profile, chores, expense statuses and agreements survive a refresh in the **same browser**.
    - A browser with no saved data shows first-run setup; malformed/unsupported saved data shows a recoverable error with a user-confirmed reset rather than a blank or crashed app.
    - Changes on one browser/device are not described or represented as synchronized elsewhere.
    
    **FR-03 — Reset/start over**
    - **Reset demo** restores original sample household data, after a confirmation explaining that local changes will be lost.
    - **Start over** clears the current household after a confirmation and returns to the first-run setup. Both actions work without server requests.
    
    ### 5.2 Household and roommates
    
    **FR-04 — Household settings**
    - Household name can be edited (trimmed, non-empty, max 60 characters).
    - Household currency can be chosen from **CAD, USD, EUR, GBP**; default CAD. All financial records use **one household currency**. Currency change is allowed only when **no expenses exist** (including settled expenses); show the reason when blocked. No exchange-rate conversion.
    
    **FR-05 — Roster and avatars**
    - Add, edit, remove-from-active-roster (archive), and restore roommates; maintain **2–5 active members**. Name is required, trimmed, 1–40 characters.
    - Show avatar initials or a selectable built-in icon/emoji; optionally allow a small uploaded image that is resized/compressed and saved locally (max stored thumbnail about 128 px; gracefully reject invalid/oversized images). No cloud upload or external image dependency.
    - Active roommates are eligible for new chore assignments, payer entries and expense splits. Historical records retain references to archived roommates.
    # Local preview
    
    For the `portable` profile, selected whenever `SITES_MANAGED_LINUX_CONTAINER` is not `1`, including on Linux devices.
    
    In a visible task with a user-facing preview tool, run the project's dev script or a static HTTP server (preferably with live reload) in a retained session after any required installation. Check that the representative page returns a successful HTTP response, then open the server's printed Local URL with `open_in_codex` or equivalent. Use supported forwarding when execution is remote; loopback on another host is not a device preview.
    
    Reuse the server and Site tab through edits and publication. For a background task or an environment without user-facing preview, start a server only when needed for the work. Request network permissions when required for the server and its readiness check. Stop the owned server during final teardown.

    import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from "react";
    
    type Variant = "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger";
    export function buttonStyles(variant: Variant = "primary", className = "") {
      const variants: Record<Variant, string> = {
        primary: "border-transparent bg-accent text-white hover:bg-accent-hover",
        secondary: "border-line-strong bg-page text-ink hover:bg-subtle",
        ghost: "border-transparent text-muted hover:bg-hover hover:text-ink",
        danger: "border-transparent bg-danger text-white hover:brightness-90",
      };
      return `inline-flex min-h-11 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-[7px] border px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium transition-colors disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 ${variants[variant]} ${className}`;
    }
    
    export function Button({ variant = "primary", className, type = "button", ...props }: ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { variant?: Variant }) {
      return <button type={type} className={buttonStyles(variant, className)} {...props} />;
    }

    "use client";
    
    import { useEffect, useId, useRef, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import { X } from "lucide-react";
    import { Button } from "./button";
    
    type DialogProps = { open: boolean; onClose: () => void; title: string; description?: string; children: ReactNode; variant?: "modal" | "drawer"; id?: string };
    
    export function Dialog({ open, onClose, title, description, children, variant = "modal", id }: DialogProps) {
      const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);
      const titleId = useId();
      const descriptionId = useId();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const dialog = dialogRef.current;
        if (!dialog || !open) return;
        const trigger = document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement ? document.activeElement : null;
        dialog.showModal();
        return () => {
          dialog.close();
          if (trigger?.isConnected) trigger.focus();
        };
      }, [open]);
    
      return (
        <dialog
          ref={dialogRef}
          id={id}
          aria-labelledby={titleId}
          aria-describedby={description ? descriptionId : undefined}
          onCancel={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); onClose(); }}
          className={`fixed flex-col overflow-hidden border border-line bg-page p-0 text-ink shadow-xl ${variant === "drawer" ? "inset-y-0 left-0 m-0 h-dvh max-h-dvh w-80 max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] rounded-r-xl" : "inset-0 m-auto max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] w-[calc(100%-2rem)] max-w-lg rounded-xl"}`}
        >
          <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center justify-between gap-4 border-b border-line px-5 py-3">
            <h2 id={titleId} className="text-lg font-semibold">{title}</h2>
            <Button variant="ghost" onClick={onClose} aria-label={`Close ${title}`} title="Close" className="size-11 shrink-0 px-0"><X aria-hidden="true" className="size-5" /></Button>
          </div>
          <div className="overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain p-5">
            {description && <p id={descriptionId} className="mb-5 text-sm text-muted">{description}</p>}
            {children}
          </div>
        </dialog>
      );
    }
    
    export function ConfirmDialog({ open, onClose, onConfirm, title, description, confirmLabel, destructive = false }: Omit<DialogProps, "children" | "variant" | "id"> & { onConfirm: () => void; confirmLabel: string; destructive?: boolean }) {
      return (
        <Dialog open={open} onClose={onClose} title={title} description={description}>
          <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-end gap-3">
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
            <Button variant={destructive ? "danger" : "primary"} onClick={onConfirm}>{confirmLabel}</Button>
          </div>
        </Dialog>
      );
    }

    import type { InputHTMLAttributes } from "react";
    
    export const controlStyles = "w-full min-w-0 rounded-[7px] border border-control bg-page px-3 py-2.5 text-base text-ink aria-invalid:border-danger disabled:bg-subtle";
    
    export function FormField({ label, help, error, id, ...props }: InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement> & { id: string; label: string; help?: string; error?: string }) {
      const descriptions = [help && `${id}-help`, error && `${id}-error`, props["aria-describedby"]].filter(Boolean).join(" ") || undefined;
      return (
        <div className="space-y-2">
          <label htmlFor={id} className="block text-sm font-medium">{label}{props.required && <span className="text-muted"> (required)</span>}</label>
          <input {...props} id={id} className={`${controlStyles} ${props.className ?? ""}`} aria-invalid={error ? true : props["aria-invalid"]} aria-describedby={descriptions} />
          {help && <p id={`${id}-help`} className="text-sm text-muted">{help}</p>}
          {error && <p id={`${id}-error`} className="text-sm text-danger">{error}</p>}
        </div>
      );
    }

    import Link from "next/link";
    import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";
    import { useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import { BookOpen, CheckSquare, House, Info, LayoutDashboard, Menu, Settings, ShieldCheck, UsersRound, Wallet } from "lucide-react";
    import { Button } from "./ui/button";

    const navigation = [
      { href: "/", label: "Dashboard", Icon: LayoutDashboard },
      { href: "/chores", label: "Chores", Icon: CheckSquare },
      { href: "/expenses", label: "Expenses", Icon: Wallet },
      { href: "/agreements", label: "Agreements", Icon: BookOpen },
      { href: "/settings", label: "Settings", Icon: Settings },
    ];
    
    function Navigation({ onNavigate }: { onNavigate?: () => void }) {
      const pathname = usePathname();
      return (
        <nav aria-label="Main navigation" className="flex flex-col gap-1">
          {navigation.map(({ href, label, Icon }) => {
            const active = pathname === href || pathname === `${href}/`;
            return (
              <Link key={href} href={href} onClick={onNavigate} aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined} className={`flex min-h-11 items-center gap-3 rounded-[7px] px-3 text-sm font-medium transition-colors ${href === "/settings" ? "mt-6" : ""} ${active ? "bg-selected text-accent" : "text-muted hover:bg-hover hover:text-ink"}`}>
                <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="size-[18px] shrink-0" />{label}
              </Link>
            );
          })}
        </nav>
      );
    }
    
    export function AppShell({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
      const pathname = usePathname();
      const [drawerPath, setDrawerPath] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [aboutOpen, setAboutOpen] = useState(false);
      const currentPage = navigation.find((item) => item.href === pathname || `${item.href}/` === pathname)?.label ?? "RoomieOS";

              <Button variant="ghost" className="w-full justify-start px-0 text-xs" onClick={() => setAboutOpen(true)}><Info aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />About this prototype</Button>

    } satisfies Record<string, { title: string; description: string; Icon: LucideIcon; emptyTitle: string; body: string }>;
    
    export function FoundationScreen({ section }: { section: keyof typeof sections }) {
      const { title, description, Icon, emptyTitle, body } = sections[section];
      return <><PageHeader title={title} description={description} icon={<Icon className="size-6" />} /><EmptyState icon={<Icon className="size-6" />} title={emptyTitle} action={<Link href="/welcome" className={buttonStyles("secondary")}>About household setup</Link>}><p>{body}</p></EmptyState><div className="mt-6"><InlineNotice>Foundation preview · This screen has no household data yet.</InlineNotice></div></>;
    }
    
    export function FoundationDashboard() {
      return (
        <>
          <PageHeader title="Your shared home, organized." description="A calmer way to share your space." icon={<House className="size-6" />} />
          <section className="rounded-[10px] border border-line p-6 sm:p-8">
            <span className="text-xs font-medium text-accent">Welcome to RoomieOS</span>
            <h2 className="mt-3 text-xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-2xl">Less keeping track. More feeling at home.</h2>
            <p className="mt-3 max-w-xl text-base text-muted">One thoughtful workspace for the chores, shared purchases and small agreements that keep a household running.</p>
            <Link href="/welcome" className={buttonStyles("primary", "mt-6")}>About household setup</Link>
          </section>
          <div className="mt-10 grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-3 md:gap-5">
            {[
              { href: "/chores", title: "Share the everyday", text: "A clear place for chores, due dates and whose turn comes next.", Icon: CheckSquare },
              { href: "/expenses", title: "Make spending clear", text: "See who paid, how costs are shared and what remains outstanding.", Icon: Wallet },
              { href: "/agreements", title: "Find common ground", text: "Keep your household's expectations easy to find and understand.", Icon: BookOpen },
            ].map(({ href, title, text, Icon }) => <Link href={href} key={href} className="group rounded-[10px] border border-transparent p-3 transition-colors hover:border-line hover:bg-subtle"><Icon aria-hidden="true" className="mb-4 size-5 text-muted" /><h2 className="text-base font-semibold group-hover:text-accent">{title}</h2><p className="mt-2 text-sm leading-relaxed text-muted">{text}</p></Link>)}
          </div>
          <div className="mt-10 border-t border-line pt-6"><InlineNotice>Foundation preview · Navigation and layout are ready. Sample and empty household setup, personal summaries and browser saving are next.</InlineNotice></div>
        </>
      );
    }
    Add: /home/csanchez/Projects/roomieos/src/state/README.md
    # Household state boundary
    
    Milestone 2 adds a single client provider here, mounted above household routes so navigation preserves state. It owns validated `AppState` facts, typed commands and the `roomieos:v1` storage adapter. Feature components keep temporary form drafts locally. Domain functions remain independent of React and storage; selectors derive balances and counts.
    
    Milestone 1 deliberately does not read or write browser household storage. No provider or seed state is installed until validation and recovery are implemented together.

    -# roomieos
    +# RoomieOS
    +
    +Your shared home, organized. An ENTI 407 client-side household prototype built with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Lucide.
    +
    +## Local development
    +
    +Use Node.js 22.12 or newer and npm:
    +
    +```sh
    +npm ci
    +npm run dev
    +```
    +
    +Open <http://localhost:3000>. The current milestone includes the responsive app shell and informative foundation screens. Household setup, profile switching and local persistence are the next milestone; this version does not initialize or modify household storage.
    +
    +## Checks
    +
    +```sh
    +npm run lint
    +npm run typecheck
    +npm test
    +npm run build
    +npm run test:browser
    +```
    +
    +Vitest is configured for future domain/storage tests; it currently permits an empty suite. Browser tests cover navigation, responsive overflow and native-dialog keyboard behavior at 375, 768 and 1280 px. Install Playwright Chromium once with `npx playwright install chromium`, or use an existing compatible Chromium executable:
    +
    +```sh
    +CHROMIUM_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium-browser npm run test:browser
    +```
    +
    +The browser suite starts its own local dev server. Screenshots and failure traces are saved under the ignored `test-results/` directory.
    +
    +## Structure and deployment
    +
    +- `src/app`: static App Router pages and household route-group layout.
    +- `src/components`: shared shell and UI primitives.
    +- `src/features`: feature views; foundation views will be replaced incrementally.
    +- `src/domain`: serializable types and, in later milestones, pure domain utilities.
    +- `src/state`: reserved boundary for the household provider and storage adapter.
    +- `src/styles`: design tokens mapped into Tailwind.
    +
    +`npm run build` exports static files to `out/`, suitable for Vercel. There are no backend API routes, server mutations, remote fonts or service integrations. No deployment is performed by the foundation scripts.
    +
    +Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [PLAN.md](PLAN.md), [PRD](docs/PRD.md) and [DESIGN](docs/DESIGN.md) before implementation. PLAN tracks verified progress; PRD and DESIGN remain authoritative for behavior and UI/UX.

    import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
    
    async function openNavigationIfNeeded(page: Page) {
      const trigger = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      if (await trigger.isVisible()) await trigger.click();
    }
    
    async function expectNoPageOverflow(page: Page) {
      const overflow = await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth);
      expect(overflow).toBe(false);
    }
    
    test("all household routes navigate, reload and fit the viewport", async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
      const errors: string[] = [];
      page.on("pageerror", (error) => errors.push(error.message));
      await page.goto("/");
      await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText("Your shared home, organized.");
      await expectNoPageOverflow(page);
      await page.screenshot({ path: testInfo.outputPath("dashboard.png"), fullPage: true });
    
      for (const [label, heading, path] of [
        ["Chores", "Chores", "/chores/"],
        ["Expenses", "Expenses", "/expenses/"],
        ["Agreements", "House agreements", "/agreements/"],
        ["Settings", "Settings", "/settings/"],
        ["Dashboard", "Your shared home, organized.", "/"],
      ]) {
        await openNavigationIfNeeded(page);
        await page.getByRole("navigation", { name: "Main navigation" }).filter({ visible: true }).getByRole("link", { name: label, exact: true }).click();
        await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`${path}$`));
        await expect(page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Navigation", exact: true })).not.toBeVisible();
        await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(heading);
        await page.reload();
        await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(heading);
        await expectNoPageOverflow(page);
      }
      expect(errors).toEqual([]);
    });
    
    test("about dialog traps keyboard focus, closes with Escape and restores focus", async ({ page }) => {
      await page.goto("/");
      await openNavigationIfNeeded(page);
      await page.getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true }).filter({ visible: true }).click();
      const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "About RoomieOS", exact: true });
      const close = dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Close About RoomieOS" });
      await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
      await expect(close).toBeFocused();
      await page.keyboard.press("Tab");
      // Native dialogs may focus the document between cycles, but never an outside control.
      expect(await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement === document.body || Boolean(document.activeElement?.closest("dialog[open]")))).toBe(true);
      await page.keyboard.press("Shift+Tab");
      await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
      await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();
      const expectedFocus = page.viewportSize()!.width >= 1024
        ? page.getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true }).filter({ visible: true })
        : page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      await expect(expectedFocus).toBeFocused();
    });
    
    test("welcome is informative and existing browser data remains untouched", async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
      const saved = JSON.stringify({ sentinel: "Milestone 1 must not initialize or overwrite state" });
      await page.addInitScript((value) => { localStorage.setItem("roomieos:v1", value); }, saved);
      await page.goto("/welcome/");
      await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Explore a sample household" })).toBeVisible();
      await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Start from scratch" })).toBeVisible();
      await expectNoPageOverflow(page);
      await page.screenshot({ path: testInfo.outputPath("welcome.png"), fullPage: true });
      await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Back to workspace" }).click();
      await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText("Your shared home, organized.");
      await page.reload();
      expect(await page.evaluate(() => localStorage.getItem("roomieos:v1"))).toBe(saved);
    });
    
    test("navigation drawer closes with Escape and returns focus", async ({ page }) => {
      test.skip(test.info().project.name === "desktop", "Desktop uses the sidebar.");
      await page.goto("/");
      const trigger = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      await trigger.click();
      await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
      await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
      await expect(page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Navigation", exact: true })).not.toBeVisible();
      await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
      await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    });

    #!/usr/bin/bash
    #
    # Copyright (c) 2011 The Chromium Authors. All rights reserved.
    # Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style license that can be
    # found in the LICENSE file.
    
    # Let the wrapped binary know that it has been run through the wrapper.
    export CHROME_WRAPPER="`readlink -f "$0"`"
    
    HERE="`dirname "$CHROME_WRAPPER"`"
    
    # We include some xdg utilities next to the binary, and we want to prefer them
    # over the system versions when we know the system versions are very old. We
    # detect whether the system xdg utilities are sufficiently new to be likely to
    # work for us by looking for xdg-settings. If we find it, we leave $PATH alone,
    # so that the system xdg utilities (including any distro patches) will be used.
    if ! which xdg-settings &> /dev/null; then
      # Old xdg utilities. Prepend $HERE to $PATH to use ours instead.
      export PATH="$HERE:$PATH"
    else
      # Use system xdg utilities. But first create mimeapps.list if it doesn't
      # exist; some systems have bugs in xdg-mime that make it fail without it.
      xdg_app_dir="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/applications}"
      mkdir -p "$xdg_app_dir"
      [ -f "$xdg_app_dir/mimeapps.list" ] || touch "$xdg_app_dir/mimeapps.list"
    fi
    
    export CHROME_VERSION_EXTRA="Built from source for Fedora release 44 (Forty Four)"
    
    # We don't want bug-buddy intercepting our crashes. http://crbug.com/24120
    export GNOME_DISABLE_CRASH_DIALOG=SET_BY_GOOGLE_CHROME
    
    # Allow users to override command-line options and prefer user defined
    # CHROMIUM_USER_FLAGS from env over system wide CHROMIUM_FLAGS
    [[ -f /etc/chromium/chromium.conf ]] && . /etc/chromium/chromium.conf
    CHROMIUM_FLAGS=${CHROMIUM_USER_FLAGS:-$CHROMIUM_FLAGS}
    
    CHROMIUM_DISTRO_FLAGS=" --enable-plugins \
                            --enable-extensions \
                            --enable-user-scripts \
                            --enable-printing \
                            --enable-sync \
                            --auto-ssl-client-auth "
    
    # Sanitize std{in,out,err} because they'll be shared with untrusted child
    # processes (http://crbug.com/376567).
    exec < /dev/null
    exec > >(exec cat)
    exec 2> >(exec cat >&2)
    
    exec -a "$0" "$HERE/chromium-browser" $CHROMIUM_FLAGS $CHROMIUM_DISTRO_FLAGS "$@"

    ```import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
    
    async function openNavigationIfNeeded(page: Page) {
      const trigger = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      if (await trigger.isVisible()) await trigger.click();
    }
    
    async function expectNoPageOverflow(page: Page) {
      const overflow = await page.evaluate(
        () => document.documentElement.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth,
      );
      expect(overflow).toBe(false);
    }
    
    test("all household routes navigate, reload and fit the viewport", async ({
      page,
    }, testInfo) => {
      const errors: string[] = [];
      page.on("pageerror", (error) => errors.push(error.message));
      await page.goto("/");
      await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(
        "Your shared home, organized.",
      );
      await expectNoPageOverflow(page);
      await page.screenshot({
        path: testInfo.outputPath("dashboard.png"),
        fullPage: true,
      });
    
      for (const [label, heading, path] of [
        ["Chores", "Chores", "/chores/"],
        ["Expenses", "Expenses", "/expenses/"],
        ["Agreements", "House agreements", "/agreements/"],
        ["Settings", "Settings", "/settings/"],
        ["Dashboard", "Your shared home, organized.", "/"],
      ]) {
        await openNavigationIfNeeded(page);
        await page
          .getByRole("navigation", { name: "Main navigation" })
          .filter({ visible: true })
          .getByRole("link", { name: label, exact: true })
          .click();
        await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`${path}$`));
        await expect(
          page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Navigation", exact: true }),
        ).not.toBeVisible();
        await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(heading);
        await page.reload();
        await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(heading);
        await expectNoPageOverflow(page);
      }
      expect(errors).toEqual([]);
    });
    
    test("about dialog traps keyboard focus, closes with Escape and restores focus", async ({
      page,
    }) => {
      await page.goto("/");
      await openNavigationIfNeeded(page);
      await page
        .getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true })
        .filter({ visible: true })
        .click();
      const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog", {
        name: "About RoomieOS",
        exact: true,
      });
      const close = dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Close About RoomieOS" });
      await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
      await expect(close).toBeFocused();
      await page.keyboard.press("Tab");
      // Native dialogs may focus the document between cycles, but never an outside control.
      expect(
        await page.evaluate(
          () =>
            document.activeElement === document.body ||
            Boolean(document.activeElement?.closest("dialog[open]")),
        ),
      ).toBe(true);
      await page.keyboard.press("Shift+Tab");
      await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
      await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();
      const expectedFocus =
        page.viewportSize()!.width >= 1024
          ? page
              .getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true })
              .filter({ visible: true })
          : page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      await expect(expectedFocus).toBeFocused();
    });
    
    test("welcome is informative and existing browser data remains untouched", async ({
      page,
    }, testInfo) => {
      const saved = JSON.stringify({
        sentinel: "Milestone 1 must not initialize or overwrite state",
      });
      await page.addInitScript((value) => {

    "use client";
    
    import Link from "next/link";
    import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";
    import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import {
      BookOpen,
      CheckSquare,
      House,
      Info,
      LayoutDashboard,
      Menu,
      Settings,
      ShieldCheck,
      UsersRound,
      Wallet,
    } from "lucide-react";
    import { Button } from "./ui/button";
    import { Dialog } from "./ui/dialog";
    import { Wordmark } from "./wordmark";
    
    const navigation = [
      { href: "/", label: "Dashboard", Icon: LayoutDashboard },
      { href: "/chores", label: "Chores", Icon: CheckSquare },
      { href: "/expenses", label: "Expenses", Icon: Wallet },
      { href: "/agreements", label: "Agreements", Icon: BookOpen },
      { href: "/settings", label: "Settings", Icon: Settings },
    ];
    
    function Navigation({ onNavigate }: { onNavigate?: () => void }) {
      const pathname = usePathname();
      return (
        <nav aria-label="Main navigation" className="flex flex-col gap-1">
          {navigation.map(({ href, label, Icon }) => {
            const active = pathname === href || pathname === `${href}/`;
            return (
              <Link
                key={href}
                href={href}
                onClick={onNavigate}
                aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}
                className={`flex min-h-11 items-center gap-3 rounded-[7px] px-3 text-sm font-medium transition-colors ${href === "/settings" ? "mt-6" : ""} ${active ? "bg-selected text-accent" : "text-muted hover:bg-hover hover:text-ink"}`}
              >
                <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="size-[18px] shrink-0" />
                {label}
              </Link>
            );
          })}
        </nav>
      );
    }
    
    export function AppShell({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
      const pathname = usePathname();
      const [drawerPath, setDrawerPath] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [aboutOpen, setAboutOpen] = useState(false);
      const currentPage =
        navigation.find(
          (item) => item.href === pathname || `${item.href}/` === pathname,
        )?.label ?? "RoomieOS";
      const drawerOpen = drawerPath === pathname;
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const desktop = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1024px)");
        const closeOnDesktop = () => {
          if (desktop.matches) setDrawerPath(null);
        };
        desktop.addEventListener("change", closeOnDesktop);
        return () => desktop.removeEventListener("change", closeOnDesktop);
      }, []);
    
      return (
        <div className="min-h-dvh lg:pl-[248px]">
          <a
            href="#main-content"
            className="fixed top-3 left-3 z-50 -translate-y-24 rounded-[7px] bg-accent px-4 py-3 text-sm font-medium text-white focus:translate-y-0"
          >
            Skip to content
          </a>
          <aside
            className="fixed inset-y-0 left-0 hidden w-[248px] flex-col border-r border-line bg-sidebar px-4 py-6 lg:flex"
            aria-label="Sidebar"
          >
            <Link
              href="/"
              aria-label="RoomieOS dashboard"
              className="mb-10 ml-2 inline-flex self-start"
            >
              <Wordmark />
            </Link>
            <p className="mb-3 px-3 text-xs font-medium text-muted">
              Your household workspace
            </p>
            <Navigation />
            <div className="mt-auto space-y-4 px-2 pt-8">
              <div className="flex items-start gap-2.5 text-sm text-muted">
                <ShieldCheck
                  aria-hidden="true"
                  className="mt-0.5 size-4 shrink-0"
                />
                <div>
                  <p className="font-medium text-ink">Local prototype</p>
                  <p className="mt-1 text-xs leading-relaxed">
                    One browser. One shared home.
                  </p>
                </div>
              </div>
              <Button
                variant="ghost"
                className="w-full justify-start px-0 text-xs"
                onClick={() => setAboutOpen(true)}
              >
                <Info aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
                About this prototype
              </Button>
            </div>
          </aside>
    
          <header className="flex min-h-14 items-center justify-between gap-3 border-b border-line px-4 sm:px-5 lg:px-10">
            <div className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-3">
              <Button
                variant="ghost"
                className="size-11 shrink-0 px-0 lg:hidden"
                aria-label="Open navigation"
                aria-expanded={drawerOpen}
                aria-controls="mobile-navigation"
                onClick={() => setDrawerPath(pathname)}
              >
                <Menu aria-hidden="true" className="size-5" />
              </Button>

    import type { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from "react";
    
    type Variant = "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "danger";
    export function buttonStyles(variant: Variant = "primary", className = "") {
      const variants: Record<Variant, string> = {
        primary: "border-transparent bg-accent text-white hover:bg-accent-hover",
        secondary: "border-line-strong bg-page text-ink hover:bg-subtle",
        ghost: "border-transparent text-muted hover:bg-hover hover:text-ink",
        danger: "border-transparent bg-danger text-white hover:brightness-90",
      };
      return `inline-flex min-h-11 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-[7px] border px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium transition-colors disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50 ${variants[variant]} ${className}`;
    }
    
    export function Button({
      variant = "primary",
      className,
      type = "button",
      ...props
    }: ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> & { variant?: Variant }) {
      return (
        <button
          type={type}
          className={buttonStyles(variant, className)}
          {...props}
        />
      );
    }

    # RoomieOS — Codex repository instructions
    
    ## Mission and source of truth
    
    Build **RoomieOS**, a polished, accessible **client-side prototype** for university students living with roommates. The app coordinates chores, shared expenses and household agreements. It is an ENTI 407 Creation Project with a Friday, 27 November 2026 deadline.
    
    Read the relevant sections of:
    - `docs/PRD.md` — product requirements, decisions, invariants and acceptance criteria. **Authoritative for behavior.**
    - `docs/DESIGN.md` — visual language, navigation, components and responsive behavior. **Authoritative for UI/UX.**
    - `PLAN.md` — approved architecture, implementation milestones, decisions and verification progress. **Authoritative for sequencing and progress.**
    
    These files contain the agreed decisions. Don't redesign features based on assumptions, or rewrite these documents unless the user explicitly asks. For a small scoped change, consult only the relevant sections rather than repeatedly reading every line.
    
    Read `PLAN.md` before implementation. Follow its approved milestones and update progress, actual verification results, blockers and approved decisions after each working slice. `docs/PRD.md` remains authoritative for behavior and `docs/DESIGN.md` for UI/UX; `PLAN.md` governs sequencing and progress. Surface conflicts rather than inventing requirements or silently expanding scope. Do not mark unchecked behavior as verified. Routine progress updates to `PLAN.md` are expected; changes to approved scope or decisions require user approval.
    
    ## Hard scope constraints
    
    - Stack: **Next.js + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Lucide icons (`lucide-react`)**; deploy on **Vercel**.
    - Persist a single versioned household in **browser `localStorage`**, key `roomieos:v1`.
    - **No backend, database service, authentication, user accounts, cloud storage, WebSockets, API keys, third-party AI, analytics or network integrations.**
    - **No fake collaboration.** A profile switcher represents a *local demo perspective*, not a real authenticated roommate.
    - **No actual money transfers.** Expense settlement is a manual whole-expense marker; don't imply an integrated payment system.
    - One household; **2–5 active roommates**. First-run must explicitly offer **sample household** or **empty household setup**.
    - Essential screens: Dashboard, Chores (List + Kanban), Expenses, Agreements, Settings, and first-run Welcome.
    - Household currency (CAD, USD, EUR, GBP) is chosen by the user; no exchange-rate calculation. Block currency changes while any expenses exist.
    - No activity feed, scheduled/background jobs, push notifications, drag-and-drop dependency, or additional features beyond PRD without approval.
    
    ## Rules that must not be broken
    
    1. **Do all expense arithmetic in integer cents.** Payer contributions and participant shares must separately sum exactly to total. Never use floating-point totals for stored financial amounts.
    2. Support **multiple payers** and all three participant split modes: equal, percentage, fixed. Use deterministic cent-allocation and validate every form.
    3. Only **open** expenses contribute to member net balances. `memberNet = totalPaid - totalShare`. Sum of nets must be zero. Debt simplification should preserve amounts and avoid invented payments.
    4. **Settling an expense means fully resolved outside the app**, excludes its net from outstanding balances, retains the record, and can be undone.
    5. Chore states are **pending, completed, skipped**. Completing writes an immutable completion event containing who and when; reopening/rotation doesn't delete history.
    6. Manual chore rotation walks the **stable active roommate roster order**, wraps around, reopens the chore as Pending and asks/confirms a new due date.
    7. Archive an active roommate only if >=2 active remain and the member has **no pending assigned chores or unsettled expense participation/contribution**. Historical records keep member identity; archived members are excluded from new selections.
    8. Every important change persists after refresh in the same browser. Refresh must not overwrite a visitor's modifications with seed data.
    9. Handle invalid input and storage failure gracefully; never silently corrupt saved state.
    10. Do not introduce dead buttons, placeholder interactions, fabricated dashboard statistics, or UI claims that contradict the local-only prototype.
    
    ## Implementation approach
    
    - Favor a clear structure (pages/features/components/domain utilities/state) over unnecessary layers, abstractions or frameworks.
    - Use typed, serializable state with `schemaVersion: 1`. Validate data on load and recover with a user-visible choice if the stored payload is invalid.
    - Put financial splitting, netting and chore rotation in **pure functions**; keep UI components thin.
    - Keep a single source of truth for the household state. Derived totals, balances and dashboard counts must be calculated from state, not persisted redundantly.
    - Use semantic HTML, accessible labeled forms and keyboard-operable dialogs. Maintain desktop and mobile usability.
    - Prefer reuse of a small set of components: app shell, member avatar/picker, modal, forms, status pill, table/cards, empty state.
    - Seed realistic *valid* demo data only when selected or reset. Use relative dates to keep overdue examples meaningful.
    - Avatar upload is optional and lower priority; initials/icons must always work without uploads or remote image URLs.
    - Avoid dependencies that are not justified for a four-day prototype.
    
    ## Workflow when implementing a task
    
    1. Identify the requested feature and consult the relevant PRD/DESIGN sections. **If the user says plan only, do not modify files.**
    2. Briefly state the intended files/behavior when the change is substantial; implement a narrow, testable slice.
    3. Test the change: run available project scripts (`npm run build`, tests, lint/typecheck if configured). Don't claim commands ran unless they actually ran.
    4. For expense math, test cent rounding, multiple payers, custom percentage/fixed splits, zero-sum nets, settlement/reopen and invalid totals.
    5. For chores, test completion history, rotation wraparound, archived members and overdue date comparisons.
    6. Manually outline UI checks the user should perform (especially refresh, empty state, Kanban, and mobile).
    7. Report succinctly: what changed, test results, known limitations, and the next suitable slice. If blocked, explain precisely.
    8. Preserve working functionality. Make small focused edits; do not casually rewrite unrelated modules.
    
    ## Suggested delivery order
    
    1. Project scaffold, visual shell, welcome sample/empty setup, household roster, local persistence.
    2. Chores CRUD, status/history, rotation, list/Kanban, overdue.
    3. Expenses CRUD, all contribution/split modes, cents math, simplified balances and settlement.
    4. Dashboard integration, agreements, settings, confirmations and reset.
    5. Responsive/accessibility polish, build/test verification, deploy.
    
    The PRD's must-have correctness and course deliverables outrank optional styling extras. Prioritize a usable, complete app by Thursday, leaving Friday as a buffer.
    
    ## Git and submission hygiene
    
    - Keep changes reviewable. Prefer commits at working milestones; **do not run destructive Git commands or overwrite user changes** without permission.
    - Never commit secrets, credentials or irrelevant personal data. No secrets are required by this project.
    - The course requests **the complete dated conversation with the AI builder** as a prompt log. Do **not** fabricate, summarize in place of, or retroactively invent prompts or dates. The user should export/save the **real Codex session transcript** from their Codex environment and review it before submission. `docs/PRD.md` and `docs/DESIGN.md` may accompany the log as appendices.
    - A passing build isn't proof of perfect UX: make it easy to verify functionality manually in a browser.

    # RoomieOS implementation plan
    
    **Last updated:** 23 November 2026
    
    **Status:** Milestone 1 implemented and verified locally; no deployment performed.
    
    **Current milestone:** Milestone 1 — foundation complete.
    
    **Next milestone:** Milestone 2 — setup and validated local persistence.
    
    **Delivery target:** Thursday, 26 November 2026; Friday, 27 November is the submission/fix buffer.
    
    ## 1. Purpose, authority and decisions
    
    Build a polished Next.js client-side prototype for ENTI 407. `docs/PRD.md` is authoritative for behavior; `docs/DESIGN.md` is authoritative for UI/UX. This document records approved architecture, sequencing and actual progress. It does not override those requirements.
    
    At plan approval, the repository contained documentation and a README, with no application scaffold. The foundation is now implemented; see the progress record below. Update this record after each working slice: check only completed work, record actual verification, and keep the current/next milestone accurate. Surface conflicts or new scope for user review rather than inventing requirements.
    
    ### Resolved requirements and defaults
    
    - **Backend conflict resolved:** The user selected the approved local-only scope. Use Next.js App Router without backend API routes, Server Actions, authentication or a database. Household operations run in the browser.
    - **History ordering:** Preserve completion events in append order; display newest first, as DESIGN specifies.
    - **Archived-member edge cases:** Historical records remain viewable and editable without losing member references. Before reopening an expense involving archived members, require their restoration. Before reopening a chore assigned to an archived member, require reassignment to an active member. Rotation can directly select the next active member.
    - **Design contrast:** Preserve the visual palette, but use sufficiently dark text variants where muted tokens fail contrast requirements.
    - **Priority:** All PRD must-haves remain MVP requirements. Defer photo uploads, drag-and-drop and decorative animation.
    
    ## 2. Architecture and state
    
    Use Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and `lucide-react`, with static deployment on Vercel.
    
    ### Application structure
    
    - **Routes (`src/app`):** `/` for Dashboard, plus `/welcome`, `/chores`, `/expenses`, `/agreements` and `/settings`. A client initialization gate shows loading until storage is read, then presents setup, recovery or the requested screen.
    - **Shared UI (`src/components`, `src/styles`):** App shell, page header, avatar/picker, fields, status pills, accessible dialogs, confirmations, notices and empty states. Desktop sidebar; mobile navigation drawer. Tables become cards on phones; Kanban scrolls within its own region.
    - **Feature modules (`src/features`):** Setup, household, chores, expenses, agreements and dashboard. Keep form drafts local to their feature.
    - **Domain utilities (`src/domain`):** Types, runtime validation, money parsing/allocation, balances, rotation, date helpers and sample generation. These functions must not depend on React or browser storage.
    - **State layer (`src/state`):** One client provider with typed domain actions and shared selectors. Route changes must preserve the provider. Keep browser storage access behind a small adapter.
    
    Follow the PRD's `AppState` model with `schemaVersion: 1`. Use stable IDs and member ordering; retain archived members. Persist facts, selected profile and settings. Calculate balances, transfer suggestions, overdue indicators and dashboard counts from those facts.
    
    ### Important interfaces
    
    - Domain actions cover CRUD, status changes, rotation, archive/restore, profile selection and resets.
    - Commands return success or actionable validation/storage errors.
    - Storage exposes load, save and clear operations with explicit failure results.
    - Inject time and ID generation into domain operations where needed for deterministic tests.
    
    ### Financial rules
    
    - Parse currency input as decimal strings into integer cents; percentages into integer basis points.
    - Require safe integer amounts and reject inputs whose calculations exceed supported integer bounds.
    - Allocate equal-split remainder cents by stable roster order. Use largest remainder for percentages, with the same stable tie-breaker.
    - Validate payer and participant totals independently. Reject duplicate entries for the same member within each role.
    - Generate advisory transfers from open-expense nets, matching largest balances first with stable member-ID ties.
    - Settlement is a confirmed whole-expense marker for resolution outside the app, never an integrated payment action.
    
    ## 3. Persistence and recovery
    
    Use only `localStorage["roomieos:v1"]`.
    
    - Read storage once after client mount. Do not render household-dependent content or save defaults before initialization completes.
    - Distinguish absent data, valid data, malformed/unsupported data and unavailable storage.
    - Validate structure, references, roster constraints, dates and financial invariants on load and before persistence.
    - Generate sample data only after explicit selection or confirmed reset. Base dates on the local date at that moment.
    - For each change, calculate and validate the next state, persist it, then publish it to React. Show success only after saving succeeds.
    - If saving fails, preserve the prior household and the user's form input. Show a useful error and allow retry.
    - Invalid data remains untouched until the user confirms reset. Unsupported versions must not silently become sample data.
    - Reset demo replaces saved state only after confirmation. Start over clears it only after confirmation and successful storage removal.
    - On another tab's storage change, stop stale writes and offer reload before further editing.
    - Store calendar dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`; use timestamps for completion events. Recompute date-sensitive displays on focus and relevant interactions.
    
    ## 4. Milestones and implementation order
    
    Each milestone ends with relevant checks, a reviewable commit and a progress update here. Introduce polish with each feature rather than postponing the entire visual design until release. During intermediate milestones, hide unavailable actions instead of exposing dead buttons.
    
    | Done | Milestone | Deliverable and acceptance gate | Target |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | [x] | 0. Planning record | Save approved plan; add document precedence and progress rules to AGENTS | Monday |
    | [x] | 1. Foundation | Scaffold, design tokens, responsive shell, shared controls/dialogs, test scripts; build passes | Completed Monday |
    | [ ] | 2. Setup and persistence | Sample/empty setup, roster, profile switching, household settings, storage validation/recovery, reset/start over; refresh preserves edits | Tuesday |
    | [ ] | 3. Chores | CRUD, status/history, rotation/date confirmation, filters, List/Kanban, overdue; both views use identical state | Tuesday |
    | [ ] | 4. Expenses | Money utilities/tests first; then CRUD, multiple payers, three split modes, breakdowns, balances and settle/reopen | Wednesday |
    | [ ] | 5. Integration | Agreements CRUD, derived dashboard, complete sample data, consistent empty/error states and feedback | Wednesday |
    | [ ] | 6. Release | Accessibility/mobile checks, production build, Vercel verification, video and real prompt transcript | Thursday |

    ## 5. Dependencies, tests and risks
    
    ### Dependencies
    
    Next.js, React, React DOM, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Lucide. Add Zod for runtime validation and Vitest for domain/storage tests. Use native forms and native dialogs with tested focus handling. Avoid state libraries, chart packages, remote fonts and UI frameworks. Select compatible stable package versions during scaffolding and commit the lockfile.
    
    Foundation tooling also includes Playwright for real-browser layout/navigation/dialog checks and Prettier for source formatting. Zod remains deferred until Milestone 2 needs runtime validation. TypeScript is pinned to 6.0.3 because the installed Next.js lint tooling rejects TypeScript 7; ESLint 9 matches the upstream React plugin's supported peer range. Exact dependency versions are recorded in `package-lock.json`.
    
    ### Required verification
    
    - **Money:** 100 cents across three participants yields 34/33/33; multiple payers; percentage rounding/ties; fixed totals; invalid inputs; zero-sum nets; deterministic transfers; settlement/reopening.
    - **Chores:** Completion identity/time; repeated completion without duplicate events for unchanged status; preserved history; rotation wraparound and archived members; yesterday/today comparisons.
    - **State/storage:** Sample and empty initialization; malformed/unsupported payloads; failed reads/writes/clears; roster limits; archive guards; currency blocked by any expenses.
    - **Browser:** Refresh every major flow, switch perspective, cancel dialogs, keyboard navigation/focus restoration, error feedback and every visible action.
    - **Layout:** 375, 768 and 1280 px; contained board scrolling; usable expense forms and dialogs.
    - **Release:** Lint, typecheck, tests and production build; deployed deep links and private-window first-run behavior.
    
    ### Main risks and mitigations
    
    | Risk | Mitigation |
    |---|---|
    | Expense-form complexity and rounding | Implement pure tested arithmetic first; preview exact contributions/shares before save |
    | Storage hydration and data loss | Client initialization gate, runtime validation, explicit recovery and save-before-publish |
    | Archived historical references | Retain member records and stable order; guard reopening and new assignments |
    | Dialog accessibility and mobile density | Reuse shared primitives; check keyboard, focus and small viewports early |
    | Short deadline | Small milestones; prioritize correct required behavior; defer optional visuals/uploads |

    "use client";
    
    import { useEffect, useId, useRef, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import { X } from "lucide-react";
    import { Button } from "./button";
    
    type DialogProps = {
      open: boolean;
      onClose: () => void;
      title: string;
      description?: string;
      children: ReactNode;
      variant?: "modal" | "drawer";
      id?: string;
    };
    
    export function Dialog({
      open,
      onClose,
      title,
      description,
      children,
      variant = "modal",
      id,
    }: DialogProps) {
      const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDialogElement>(null);
      const titleId = useId();
      const descriptionId = useId();
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const dialog = dialogRef.current;
        if (!dialog || !open) return;
        const trigger =
          document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement
            ? document.activeElement
            : null;
        dialog.showModal();
        return () => {
          dialog.close();
          if (trigger?.isConnected) trigger.focus();
        };
      }, [open]);
    
      return (
        <dialog
          ref={dialogRef}
          id={id}
          aria-labelledby={titleId}
          aria-describedby={description ? descriptionId : undefined}
          onCancel={(event) => {
            event.preventDefault();
            onClose();
          }}
          className={`fixed flex-col overflow-hidden border border-line bg-page p-0 text-ink shadow-xl ${variant === "drawer" ? "inset-y-0 left-0 m-0 h-dvh max-h-dvh w-80 max-w-[calc(100%-2rem)] rounded-r-xl" : "inset-0 m-auto max-h-[calc(100dvh-2rem)] w-[calc(100%-2rem)] max-w-lg rounded-xl"}`}
        >
          <div className="flex shrink-0 items-center justify-between gap-4 border-b border-line px-5 py-3">
            <h2 id={titleId} className="text-lg font-semibold">
              {title}
            </h2>
            <Button
              variant="ghost"
              onClick={onClose}
              aria-label={`Close ${title}`}
              title="Close"
              size="icon"
            >
              <X aria-hidden="true" className="size-5" />
            </Button>
          </div>
          <div className="overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain p-5">
            {description && (
              <p id={descriptionId} className="mb-5 text-sm text-muted">
                {description}
              </p>
            )}
            {children}
          </div>
        </dialog>
      );
    }
    
    export function ConfirmDialog({
      open,
      onClose,
      onConfirm,
      title,
      description,
      confirmLabel,
      destructive = false,
    }: Omit<DialogProps, "children" | "variant" | "id"> & {
      onConfirm: () => void;
      confirmLabel: string;
      destructive?: boolean;
    }) {
      return (
        <Dialog
          open={open}
          onClose={onClose}
          title={title}
          description={description}
        >
          <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-end gap-3">
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onClose}>
              Cancel
            </Button>
            <Button
              variant={destructive ? "danger" : "primary"}
              onClick={onConfirm}
            >
              {confirmLabel}
            </Button>
          </div>
        </Dialog>
      );
    }
    import type { Metadata } from "next";
    import "./globals.css";
    
    export const metadata: Metadata = {
      title: { default: "RoomieOS", template: "%s · RoomieOS" },
      description:
        "Your shared home, organized. A local household prototype for chores, expenses and house agreements.",
    };
    
    export default function RootLayout({
      children,
    }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) {
      return (
        <html lang="en">
          <body className="min-h-dvh text-base leading-relaxed antialiased">
            {children}
          </body>
        </html>
      );
    }

    import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
    
    async function openNavigationIfNeeded(page: Page) {
      const trigger = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      if (page.viewportSize()!.width < 1024) {
        await trigger.click();
        await expect(
          page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Navigation", exact: true }),
        ).toBeVisible();
      }
    }
    
    async function expectNoPageOverflow(page: Page) {
      const overflow = await page.evaluate(
        () => document.documentElement.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth,
      );
      expect(overflow).toBe(false);
    }
    
    test("all household routes navigate, reload and fit the viewport", async ({
      page,
    }, testInfo) => {
      const errors: string[] = [];
      page.on("pageerror", (error) => errors.push(error.message));
      await page.goto("/");
      await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(
        "Your shared home, organized.",
      );
      await expectNoPageOverflow(page);
      await page.screenshot({
        path: testInfo.outputPath("dashboard.png"),
        fullPage: true,
      });
    
      for (const [label, heading, path] of [
        ["Chores", "Chores", "/chores/"],
        ["Expenses", "Expenses", "/expenses/"],
        ["Agreements", "House agreements", "/agreements/"],
        ["Settings", "Settings", "/settings/"],
        ["Dashboard", "Your shared home, organized.", "/"],
      ]) {
        await openNavigationIfNeeded(page);
        await page
          .getByRole("navigation", { name: "Main navigation" })
          .filter({ visible: true })
          .getByRole("link", { name: label, exact: true })
          .click();
        await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`${path}$`));
        await expect(
          page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Navigation", exact: true }),
        ).not.toBeVisible();
        await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(heading);
        await page.reload();
        await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })).toHaveText(heading);
        await expectNoPageOverflow(page);
      }
      expect(errors).toEqual([]);
    });
    
    test("about dialog traps keyboard focus, closes with Escape and restores focus", async ({
      page,
    }) => {
      await page.goto("/");
      await openNavigationIfNeeded(page);
      await page
        .getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true })
        .filter({ visible: true })
        .click();
      const dialog = page.getByRole("dialog", {
        name: "About RoomieOS",
        exact: true,
      });
      const close = dialog.getByRole("button", { name: "Close About RoomieOS" });
      await expect(dialog).toBeVisible();
      await expect(close).toBeFocused();
      await page.keyboard.press("Tab");
      // Native dialogs may focus the document between cycles, but never an outside control.
      expect(
        await page.evaluate(
          () =>
            document.activeElement === document.body ||
            Boolean(document.activeElement?.closest("dialog[open]")),
        ),
      ).toBe(true);
      await page.keyboard.press("Shift+Tab");
      await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
      await expect(dialog).not.toBeVisible();
      const expectedFocus =
        page.viewportSize()!.width >= 1024
          ? page
              .getByRole("button", { name: "About this prototype", exact: true })
              .filter({ visible: true })
          : page.getByRole("button", { name: "Open navigation" });
      await expect(expectedFocus).toBeFocused();
    });

    # RoomieOS
    
    Your shared home, organized. An ENTI 407 client-side household prototype built with Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Lucide.
    
    ## Local development
    
    Use Node.js 22.12 or newer and npm:
    
    ```sh
    npm ci
    npm run dev
    ```
    
    Open <http://localhost:3000>. The current milestone includes the responsive app shell and informative foundation screens. Household setup, profile switching and local persistence are the next milestone; this version does not initialize or modify household storage.
    
    ## Checks
    
    ```sh
    npm run lint
    npm run typecheck
    npm test
    npm run build
    npm run test:browser
    ```
    
    Vitest is configured for future domain/storage tests; it currently permits an empty suite. Browser tests cover navigation, responsive overflow and native-dialog keyboard behavior at 375, 768 and 1280 px. Install Playwright Chromium once with `npx playwright install chromium`, or use an existing compatible Chromium executable:
    
    ```sh
    CHROMIUM_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium-browser npm run test:browser
    ```
    
    The browser suite starts its own local dev server. Screenshots and failure traces are saved under the ignored `test-results/` directory.
    
    ## Structure and deployment
    
    - `src/app`: static App Router pages and household route-group layout.
    - `src/components`: shared shell and UI primitives.
    - `src/features`: feature views; foundation views will be replaced incrementally.
    - `src/domain`: serializable types and, in later milestones, pure domain utilities.
    - `src/state`: reserved boundary for the household provider and storage adapter.
    - `src/styles`: design tokens mapped into Tailwind.
    
    `npm run build` exports static files to `out/`, suitable for Vercel. There are no backend API routes, server mutations, remote fonts or service integrations. No deployment is performed by the foundation scripts.
    
    Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [PLAN.md](PLAN.md), [PRD](docs/PRD.md) and [DESIGN](docs/DESIGN.md) before implementation. PLAN tracks verified progress; PRD and DESIGN remain authoritative for behavior and UI/UX.

    Playwright is a testing framework that lets you automate Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with a single API. You can use it to write **End-to-End (E2E)** testing. This guide will show you how to set up Playwright with Next.js and write your first tests.
    
    ## Quickstart
    
    The fastest way to get started is to use `create-next-app` with the [with-playwright example](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-playwright). This will create a Next.js project complete with Playwright configured.
    
    ```bash package="pnpm"
    pnpm create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
    ```
    
    ```bash package="npm"
    npx create-next-app@latest --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
    ```
    
    ```bash package="yarn"
    yarn create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
    ```
    
    ```bash package="bun"
    bun create next-app --example with-playwright with-playwright-app
    ```
    
    ## Manual setup
    
    To install Playwright, run the following command:
    
    ```bash package="pnpm"
    pnpm create playwright
    ```
    
    ```bash package="npm"
    npm init playwright
    ```
    
    ```bash package="yarn"
    yarn create playwright
    ```
    
    ```bash package="bun"
    bun create playwright
    ```
    
    This will take you through a series of prompts to set up and configure Playwright for your project, including adding a `playwright.config.ts` file. Please refer to the [Playwright installation guide](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro#installation) for the step-by-step guide.

    title: Server and Client Components
    description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.
    related:
      title: Next Steps
      description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.
      links:
        - app/api-reference/directives/use-client
        - app/guides/server-and-client-boundary
    ---
    
    By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.
    
    This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.
    
    > **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).
    
    ## When to use Server and Client Components?
    
    The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.
    
    Use **Client Components** when you need:
    
    - [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`.
    - [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`.
    - Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `navigator.geolocation`, etc.
    - [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).
    
    Use **Server Components** when you need:
    
    - Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source.
    - Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client.
    - Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.
    - Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client.
    
    For example, the `<Page>` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `<LikeButton>` which handles client-side interactivity.
    
    ```tsx filename="app/[id]/page.tsx" highlight={1,17} switcher
    import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
    import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
    
    export default async function Page({
      params,
    }: {
      params: Promise<{ id: string }>
    }) {
      const { id } = await params
      const post = await getPost(id)
    
      return (
        <div>
          <main>
            <h1>{post.title}</h1>
            {/* ... */}
            <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
          </main>
        </div>
      )
    }
    ```
    
    ```jsx filename="app/[id]/page.js" highlight={1,13} switcher

            <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
          </main>
        </div>
      )
    }
    ```

    +## Hydration troubleshooting
    +
    +If the development overlay shows unexpected HTML attributes such as `bis_skin_checked` or `bis_register`, a browser extension may have modified the page before React hydrated it. Those attributes are not generated by RoomieOS. Try a fresh browser profile with extensions disabled, or a private window where no extensions are allowed. If the warning disappears, disable the responsible extension for localhost and reload. See the [Next.js hydration guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/react-hydration-error).
    +
    +Keep hydration diagnostics enabled. The route browser test checks both uncaught errors and console errors, including React hydration warnings, in an isolated browser context. If the warning persists with extensions disabled, inspect the new diff for an application mismatch.

    "use client";
    
    import Link from "next/link";
    import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";
    import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
    import {
      BookOpen,
      CheckSquare,
      House,
      Info,
      LayoutDashboard,
      Menu,
      Settings,
      ShieldCheck,
      UsersRound,
      Wallet,
    } from "lucide-react";
    import { Button } from "./ui/button";
    import { Dialog } from "./ui/dialog";
    import { Wordmark } from "./wordmark";
    
    const navigation = [
      { href: "/", label: "Dashboard", Icon: LayoutDashboard },
      { href: "/chores", label: "Chores", Icon: CheckSquare },
      { href: "/expenses", label: "Expenses", Icon: Wallet },
      { href: "/agreements", label: "Agreements", Icon: BookOpen },
      { href: "/settings", label: "Settings", Icon: Settings },
    ];
    
    function Navigation({ onNavigate }: { onNavigate?: () => void }) {
      const pathname = usePathname();
      return (
        <nav aria-label="Main navigation" className="flex flex-col gap-1">
          {navigation.map(({ href, label, Icon }) => {
            const active = pathname === href || pathname === `${href}/`;
            return (
              <Link
                key={href}
                href={href}
                onClick={onNavigate}
                aria-current={active ? "page" : undefined}
                className={`flex min-h-11 items-center gap-3 rounded-[7px] px-3 text-sm font-medium transition-colors ${href === "/settings" ? "mt-6" : ""} ${active ? "bg-selected text-accent" : "text-muted hover:bg-hover hover:text-ink"}`}
              >
                <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="size-[18px] shrink-0" />
                {label}
              </Link>
            );
          })}
        </nav>
      );
    }
    
    export function AppShell({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
      const pathname = usePathname();
      const [drawerPath, setDrawerPath] = useState<string | null>(null);
      const [aboutOpen, setAboutOpen] = useState(false);
      const currentPage =
        navigation.find(
          (item) => item.href === pathname || `${item.href}/` === pathname,
        )?.label ?? "RoomieOS";
      const drawerOpen = drawerPath === pathname;
    
      useEffect(() => {
        const desktop = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1024px)");
        const closeOnDesktop = () => {
          if (desktop.matches) setDrawerPath(null);
        };
        desktop.addEventListener("change", closeOnDesktop);
        return () => desktop.removeEventListener("change", closeOnDesktop);
      }, []);
    
      return (
        <div className="min-h-dvh lg:pl-[248px]">
          <a
            href="#main-content"
            className="fixed top-3 left-3 z-50 -translate-y-24 rounded-[7px] bg-accent px-4 py-3 text-sm font-medium text-white focus:translate-y-0"
          >
            Skip to content
          </a>
          <aside
            className="fixed inset-y-0 left-0 hidden w-[248px] flex-col border-r border-line bg-sidebar px-4 py-6 lg:flex"
            aria-label="Sidebar"
          >
            <Link
              href="/"
              aria-label="RoomieOS dashboard"
              className="mb-10 ml-2 inline-flex self-start"
            >
              <Wordmark />
            </Link>
            <p className="mb-3 px-3 text-xs font-medium text-muted">
              Your household workspace
            </p>
            <Navigation />
            <div className="mt-auto space-y-4 px-2 pt-8">
              <div className="flex items-start gap-2.5 text-sm text-muted">
                <ShieldCheck
                  aria-hidden="true"
                  className="mt-0.5 size-4 shrink-0"
                />
                <div>
                  <p className="font-medium text-ink">Local prototype</p>
                  <p className="mt-1 text-xs leading-relaxed">
                    One browser. One shared home.
                  </p>
                </div>
              </div>
              <Button
                variant="ghost"
                className="w-full justify-start text-xs"
                onClick={() => setAboutOpen(true)}
              >
                <Info aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
                About this prototype
              </Button>

    ---
    title: distDir
    description: Set a custom build directory to use instead of the default .next directory.
    ---
    
    {/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}
    
    You can specify a name to use for a custom build directory to use instead of `.next`.
    
    Open `next.config.js` and add the `distDir` config:
    
    ```js filename="next.config.js"
    module.exports = {
      distDir: 'build',
    }
    ```
    
    Now if you run `next build` Next.js will use `build` instead of the default `.next` folder.
    
    > **Good To Know:** Next.js takes ownership of `distDir` and will sometimes delete its contents. Point it at a directory used only by Next.js.
    
    `distDir` is resolved relative to the directory holding your `next.config.js`, and may
    point to a dedicated directory inside the workspace that contains it. In a monorepo, an
    application at `apps/web` can build into `../.next`.
    
    To protect against data loss, Next.js refuses to use the directory and fails with an
    [Invalid distDir](/docs/messages/invalid-dist-dir) error when `distDir` resolves outside
    the application and workspace, or when it is the application directory itself or one of
    its ancestors.
